The fault is in [internal/cmd/grpc.go](/app/internal/cmd/grpc.go:160): `NewGRPCServer` constructs the tracing resource and provider, while `getTraceExporter` selects exporters using package global state ([line 461](/app/internal/cmd/grpc.go:461)). That `sync.Once` makes later calls reuse the first configuration. The existing [exporter test](/app/internal/cmd/grpc_test.go:17) resets it before every case, so it cannot catch that behavior.

The fix should place `newResource`, `NewProvider`, and `GetExporter` in `internal/tracing/tracing.go`, then call the exported functions from server startup. Isolated coverage should check environment resource attributes, always-on sampling, all four OTLP endpoint forms and headers, invalid endpoints, unsupported exporters, repeated calls with different configs, and shutdown callbacks. Jaeger and Zipkin currently return a no-op shutdown callback; the HTTP endpoint’s transport behavior also needs verification.

I recorded the diagnosis in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`. No project source or tests were changed because this run’s specialist instructions limit it to fault localization. A network-disabled exporter test run produced no result before I interrupted the long build.

Moved tracing resource, provider, and exporter setup into [internal/tracing/tracing.go](/app/internal/tracing/tracing.go). The gRPC server now uses those functions and registers provider and exporter shutdown in its lifecycle. Exporters are created per call, so one configuration cannot be reused for a later call.

Added isolated tests for environment attributes, always-on sampling, exporter endpoints and errors, repeated calls, shutdown, and OTLP HTTP headers and path. The targeted tests passed with `GOPROXY=off`, and `git diff --check` passed.

VERDICT: FIX

[internal/tracing/tracing.go](/app/internal/tracing/tracing.go:25) applies environment attributes after `service.version`. Setting `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.version=other` can therefore replace the required `fliptVersion`. Apply the version attribute after the environment attributes, while preserving environment overrides for `service.name`, and cover this case in the existing resource test.

Tests: `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./internal/tracing ./internal/cmd` — both packages passed. No test environment problem. This was an independent review; I did not change project code.

Fixed the resource attribute order so the supplied Flipt version wins over `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, while `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` can still override the default service name. The resource test now covers the version override.

The reviewer’s exact command passed: `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./internal/tracing ./internal/cmd`.
